research_question: What is the effect of exercise therapy, compared with no treatment, usual care, or limited/minimal education, on quality of life at longer-term follow-up (up to and including 12 months post-intervention) in adults with knee osteoarthritis?
treatment_label: Exercise therapy (land- or water-based therapeutic exercise programme)
control_label: No treatment, usual care, or limited/minimal education
outcome_description: Health-related quality of life at longer-term follow-up (post-intervention follow-up assessments up to and including 12 months), measured with whichever instrument the study itself designates as its quality-of-life outcome (e.g. SF-36/SF-12 physical or mental component summary, EQ-5D index, AQoL, WOMAC/KOOS quality-of-life subscale, Nottingham Health Profile, or disease-specific QoL questionnaires). Data measured immediately at the end of the intervention period are not eligible for this timepoint.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g / SMD means the exercise group had BETTER quality of life than the no-treatment, usual-care, or limited-education control group at longer-term (up to 12-month) follow-up.
search_queries: exercise therapy knee osteoarthritis randomized controlled trial quality of life
knee osteoarthritis exercise program usual care control trial 12 month follow-up outcomes
therapeutic exercise knee OA health-related quality of life SF-36 EQ-5D trial effect
inclusion_criteria: Adults with knee osteoarthritis (clinically or radiographically diagnosed) in any setting
Study compares an exercise intervention with a non-exercise comparator such as no treatment, waiting list, usual care, or limited/minimal education
Reports some quantitative quality-of-life outcome at a follow-up assessment after the end of the intervention, up to and including 12 months
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, opinion piece, protocol, narrative or theoretical paper)

No comparison between an exercise treatment condition and an eligible control condition; comparator is an attention-control/placebo/sham condition, another active treatment, or a co-intervention design in which exercise is added on top of a treatment received by both arms

No quantitative quality-of-life outcome data usable for an effect size (no means+SDs, t/F values, confidence intervals, or equivalent), or quality-of-life data reported only at the immediate end-of-intervention timepoint with no later follow-up up to 12 months
Completely unrelated to exercise for knee osteoarthritis (e.g. hip-only or other joint populations, post-arthroplasty rehabilitation, animal or non-clinical studies)
moderators_to_extract: Intervention duration and supervision (supervised vs home-based)
Comparator type (no treatment/waitlist vs usual care vs limited education)
Length of follow-up after intervention end (months)
Sample size category and risk-of-bias rating
effect_size_note: Pool as standardized mean difference (Hedges g corrected) because studies use different quality-of-life instruments. For each study extract only the instrument the paper itself frames as its quality-of-life outcome, and only the longer-term follow-up assessment (post-intervention, up to and including 12 months); if several eligible follow-ups exist, use the one closest to 12 months. Reverse-sign scales on which higher = worse (e.g. WOMAC, Nottingham Health Profile) so that positive values always favour exercise. Random-effects (REML) model with Knapp-Hartung adjustment.
